mail.date.long.note: A date as the bridge's emails write it, such as "2 January 2027" (in the account-removal warning's subject and text). {day} is the day of the month (1 to 31), {month} the month's name (one of mail.date.january to mail.date.december), {year} the year (2027). Arrange them as your language writes a full date, adding its words or punctuation ("2 de enero de 2027", "2. Januar 2027"). {day} is a count only so that a language can write the first of the month its own way in the form one (French: "1er janvier 2027"); where that is the plain number, both forms are the same.

mail.greeting.named.note: First line of every email the bridge sends to an Off The Cloud account holder (confirming the email address, resetting the password, the account-removal warning), on its own line above the text. {name} is the person's first name as they gave it at sign-up. Plain-text email.

mail.greeting.plain.note: First line of every email the bridge sends to an Off The Cloud account holder whose name isn't known (an account made with Apple that shared no name), on its own line above the text. Plain-text email.

mail.identity.body.text:
The device name {domain} of your Off The Cloud account was just given a new identity: the device that used it until now can no longer connect to the bridge, and the name now leads to the device that has the new one.

If you did this yourself - setting a device up again with the same name, or New identity on your account page - there is nothing more to do.

If you didn't, someone else is using your account: sign in at {link}, choose Sign out everywhere and change your password, then set your own device up again with the same name.
mail.identity.body.note: Text of the email sent when one of the account's device names gets a new identity: a device set up again with that name, or New identity (site.account.domains.new_identity) on the account page. Plain text: keep the empty lines. It follows the greeting (mail.greeting.*) and is signed "- Off The Cloud" with the website's address below. {domain} is the device's address (name.off-the.cloud), {link} the account page's address. New identity and Sign out everywhere are the account page's buttons (site.account.domains.new_identity, site.account.password.sign_out_all): use their words.

mail.identity.subject.note: Subject of the email sent to an Off The Cloud account holder when one of the account's device names gets a new identity (mail.identity.body). {domain} is the device's address (name.off-the.cloud).

mail.inactivity.body.text:
Your Off The Cloud bridge account ({email}) hasn't been used for five months: no one has signed in to it, none of your devices has been connected to the bridge, and no app or friend has reached them through it.

As our terms say, an account unused for six months is removed. If nothing changes, this one and its device names will be removed on {date}. Your devices keep working at home.

To keep it, sign in at {link} or switch on one of your devices with internet access before then.
mail.inactivity.body.note: Text of the email warning that an unused account will be removed in a month, as the terms of use say. Plain text: keep the empty lines between paragraphs. It follows the greeting (mail.greeting.*) and is signed "Off The Cloud" below. {email} is the account's email address, {date} the removal date (written by mail.date.long), {link} the account page's address (https://off-the.cloud/account). The bridge is the service that gives a device its address on the internet; device names are those addresses. The devices themselves, and their files, are not affected.

mail.inactivity.subject.text: Your Off The Cloud account will be removed on {date}
mail.inactivity.subject.note: Subject of the email warning that an unused account will be removed in a month (mail.inactivity.body). {date} is the removal date, written by mail.date.long ("11 November 2026").

mail.provider_link.body.text:
You can now sign in to your Off The Cloud account ({email}) with {provider}. The account also has a password, which goes on working.

If you chose that password yourself, there is nothing more to do.

If you didn't, someone else made this account with your email address before you, and can still sign in with it: at {link}, sign out, choose Forgot your password? and set a new password. That signs everyone else out.
mail.provider_link.body.note: Text of the email sent when someone first signs in with Google or Apple to an Off The Cloud account that was made with an email and a password: the account keeps its password, which may have been set by someone who signed up with this person's address before them. Plain text: keep the empty lines. It follows the greeting (mail.greeting.plain) and is signed "- Off The Cloud" with the website's address below. {email} is the account's email address, {provider} Google or Apple (never translated), {link} the account page's address. Forgot your password? is the account page's link (site.account.forgot.open): use its words.

mail.provider_link.subject.text: {provider} sign-in added to your Off The Cloud account
mail.provider_link.subject.note: Subject of the email sent when someone first signs in with Google or Apple to an Off The Cloud account that also has a password (mail.provider_link.body). {provider} is Google or Apple, never translated.

mail.reset.body.text:
Someone - hopefully you - asked to reset the password of the Off The Cloud account for this email. To choose a new one, open this link:

{link}

The link works for one hour, once. Setting a new password signs your account out everywhere else.

If you didn't ask for this, ignore this email: your password stays as it is.
mail.reset.body.note: Text of the email sent after Forgot password on the account page (off-the.cloud/account). Plain text: keep the empty lines, and {link} on a line of its own. It follows the greeting (mail.greeting.*) and is signed "- Off The Cloud" with the website's address below. {link} is the one-time link that opens the account page to choose a new password.

mail.reset.subject.text: Reset your Off The Cloud password
mail.reset.subject.note: Subject of the email sent after Forgot password on the account page, carrying a link to choose a new password (mail.reset.body).

mail.verify.body.text:
Please confirm that this is your email address by opening this link:

{link}

The link works for 48 hours. Once your email is confirmed you can register your devices on the bridge.

If you didn't create an Off The Cloud account, ignore this email: nothing is registered for this address without the confirmation.
mail.verify.body.note: Text of the email sent after signing up for an Off The Cloud account with an email address, to confirm the address (and again when asked for). Plain text: keep the empty lines, and {link} on a line of its own. It follows the greeting (mail.greeting.*) and is signed "- Off The Cloud" with the website's address below. {link} is the confirmation link. Registering a device on the bridge gives it its address on the internet (name.off-the.cloud).

mail.verify.subject.text: Confirm your email for Off The Cloud
mail.verify.subject.note: Subject of the email sent after signing up for an Off The Cloud account with an email address, carrying the link that confirms the address (mail.verify.body).
